*The lead and the summary by thesis: 4–5 minutes to read; every row: 33–43 minutes.*

Every test in [experiments](experiments/README.md) by how it came out, the failures first: 66 in all (4 failed; 20 mixed; 2 refused before scoring; 1 decided nothing; 2 partly passed; 3 not rejected; 5 passed; 2 decided by a registered rule; 2 reported without a verdict; 11 frozen, not run; 3 held; 1 dropped; 10 no prediction of the account), as of 8 November 2026. Each row links its folder and quotes the outcome from its pages (one, where they have no sentence to quote, from method §9), the source linked; its class is read from the folder's verdicts, and its plain gloss is a restatement [AI reading]. The rows were drafted from the folders by an AI reader and checked against them by a second; no person's check of them is recorded. A row's thesis is the one method §9 or the test's folder names; Frozen is the day its prediction, rule or plan was fixed, and Run the day the run finished. Experiments retired to [experiments/history](experiments/history/INDEX.md) are not listed. T8 is argued, and no test bears on it.

How to read a verdict, in [method §9](theories/becoming/chapters/08-METHOD.md#theses)'s words: "A thesis adds no theorem, a refutation removes none, and a failure stays recorded beside the thesis." "A frozen rule fixes how a verdict is scored before the data, not that the rule reads the construct the verdict names…" "So a verdict is read against every measure of its construct the run produced, and where they disagree with the rule's print, the disagreement is reported and the verdict not claimed."

Results here are by test: each row is one test in the setting or settings it names, a thesis can pass in one and fail in another, so no row or count below is a verdict on a thesis as a whole (method §9's table gives each thesis's standing), and a row's class is read by the rule stated under that class's heading below.
